Positive atoms or an odd cycle make the inequality strict; bipartite sign conjugation gives exact edgewise opposite signs and the explicit positive atom+edge deficit. A finite triangular limiting system establishes the geometric graded-path endpoint profile and sharp family supremum. All continuous and atomic norm/equality boundary cases are checked; an exact rational checker confirms 560 finite samples and limiting-witness trends without purporting to prove infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: The result extends a classical sharp interval projector norm to connected network topologies with arbitrary edge-mass grading, despite unboundedness phenomena for distorted 2D finite-element meshes. Its sharp bipartite positive graph-specific atom/edge deficit identifies exactly the stability loss and all norming evaluation vertices; a reproducible graded-path construction shows the universal constant cannot be improved. This is an exact structural extension and a quantitative conditioning principle, not merely a special-case recomputation of the interval bound.
